paragraphs: When comparing adjacent directions, first examine scope of practice and deliverables: continuous care across all ages, adult internal medicine, child health, maternity and gynecology, emergency management, population prevention, or practice under a collaborative agreement. This occupation differs in carrying ultimate responsibility for overall patient care and incorporating preventive care and chronic disease management into long-term follow-up.

The following occupations all belong to medical and health services but have different scopes of practice and deliverables; use them to locate a direction, rather than substitute one for another. Scope of practice, prescribing authority, and training pathways for each direction must be checked against local regulations and institutional policies.
Primarily diagnosis and nonsurgical treatment of adult internal conditions; this occupation covers all ages and emphasizes continuity and preventive care
Choose that occupation if you prefer complex adult internal medicine cases; choose this occupation if you prefer continuous care and prevention across all ages
Diagnose and treat adult internal conditions and manage inpatient and outpatient cases
General Internal Medicine Physicians
Primarily clinical care and developmental assessment for infants, children, and adolescents; this occupation covers the full life cycle from childhood to old age
Choose that occupation if you prefer child health and developmental issues; choose this occupation if you prefer all-age care and whole-family care
Provide clinical care and developmental follow-up for children and adolescents
Pediatricians
Primarily maternity care, gynecological diseases, and surgery; this occupation does not undertake routine obstetric and gynecological surgery
Choose that occupation if you prefer maternity care and gynecological surgery; choose this occupation if you prefer internal medicine and general practice care
Provide maternity care and diagnose and treat gynecological diseases and perform surgery
Obstetricians and Gynecologists
Primarily immediate management and triage of acute conditions and trauma; this occupation primarily focuses on continuous outpatient care and chronic disease management
Choose that occupation if you prefer acute management and intensive duty schedules; choose this occupation if you prefer long-term follow-up and chronic disease management
Immediately assess and stabilize acutely ill patients in emergency settings
Emergency Medicine Physicians
Primarily population prevention, public health, and policy; this occupation focuses on individual clinical care and clinical preventive services
Choose that occupation if you prefer public health and population strategies; choose this occupation if you prefer individual clinical care and clinical screening
Design and implement population prevention and public health measures
Preventive Medicine Physicians
Practice under physician supervision or collaboration, with scope limited by regulations and collaborative agreements; this occupation carries ultimate clinical and prescribing responsibility
Choose that occupation if you prefer collaborative practice and a shorter training period; choose this occupation if you prefer ultimate clinical responsibility
Complete consultations, examinations, and treatment within the scope of collaboration
